Thomas 1909, Ellerman 1940 and Moore 1959 all use this character to separate Heliosciurus/Protoxerus/Epixerus from Paraxerus/Funisciurus. Ellerman 1940: zygomatic plate "constantly more strongly ridged ... in typical Heliosciurus and in Aethosciurus ruwenzorii", in contrast to the "curiously shortened zygomatic plate" of Paraxerus, Funisciurus and the other Aethosciurus. All 6 MDD species covered (H. ruwenzorii via Ellerman and Moore). Thomas 1909 places the Heliosciurus ridge AT the suture and the Protoxerus ridge BEYOND it; both are "yes" here.

zygomatic_ridge_reaches_premaxilla.notes: zygomatic_ridge_reaches_premaxilla: does the sharp anterior ridge of the zygomatic plate (upper edge of the masseteric fossa) continue forward on the rostrum to the maxillo-premaxillary suture or beyond (yes), or stop well short of the premaxilla, above the infraorbital foramen and no higher than the lower edge of the lacrimal (no)? Thomas 1909, Ellerman 1940 and Moore 1959 all use this character to separate Heliosciurus/Protoxerus/Epixerus from Paraxerus/Funisciurus. Coverage by MDD species: Moore 1959 gives it as subtribal character 1 of the Funisciurina, i.e. Funisciurus + Paraxerus including Tamiscus (boehmi group) and Aethosciurus (poensis, lucifer, vexillarius; not ruwenzori), synoptic series P. cepapi, alexandri, palliatus, boehmi (+ vulcanorum, emini, antoniae); MS 1030 repeats it for P. cepapi. Thomas 1909 Paraxerus (alexandri, boehmi, cepapi, ochraceus, palliatus and synonyms): "zygomatic ridge as in Funisciurus", whose ridge falls "far short of the maxillo-premaxillary suture". Ellerman 1940: Paraxerus (cepapi, ochraceus, palliatus, flavovittis, boehmi, alexandri, byatti = vexillarius byatti) skull "essentially as in Funisciurus"; poensis "zygomatic plate as in Paraxerus"; lucifer group (lucifer, vexillarius) "zygomatic plate ... as in poensis"; all non-ruwenzorii Aethosciurus have the "curiously shortened zygomatic plate". P. cooperi and P. vincenti (both described by Hayman 1950) are NOT individually described by any source found; they are covered only by Moore's genus/subtribe-level statement (Denys et al. 2014 note that Moore placed cooperi in Aethosciurus, which Moore includes in Paraxerus/Funisciurina). Scope "genus" rests on that.

caveats: 1) Separator found: zygomatic_ridge_reaches_premaxilla (Heliosciurus yes; Paraxerus no) is stated independently by Thomas 1909, Ellerman 1940 and Moore 1959, and corroborated for P. cepapi by Mammalian Species 1030. Coverage is explicit for all 6 Heliosciurus species and 9 of 11 Paraxerus species; P. cooperi and P. vincenti (described 1950) rest only on Moore's genus/subtribe-level diagnosis (scope "genus"). 2) sphenopalatine_foramen_size and premaxilla_dorsoanterior_process_meets_nasal come from Moore 1959 alone; the Heliosciurus/Protoxerus/Epixerus state of the premaxilla character is read from Moore's differential diagnosis (Funambulini "distinguished ... from the Protoxerini by 1") rather than from a positive description. Moore warns that Heliosciurus skull characters are unusually variable. Prefer zygomatic_ridge_reaches_premaxilla in the key. 3) tail_rings for Heliosciurus now includes "absent": Grubb 1982 documents H. mutabilis tails without discrete rings (melanistic specimens whose tail hairs lose the light bands). The union with the earlier file makes Heliosciurus tail_rings uninformative, which is the sound coding. 4) Not changed but worth knowing: Moore 1959 says the open oval infraorbital foramen of Protoxerus/Epixerus is "very closely approached also in Heliosciurus, but only in one form" (still a canal, so the earlier infraorbital_foramen_forms_canal coding stands); Moore also notes Didier (1953) figured a Sciurus-like baculum attributed to H. rufobrachium, contradicting Pocock's "no baculum" (the earlier baculum coding is partial and unused, which is appropriate). Mammae (3 pairs in both H. rufobrachium and P. cepapi) do not separate the genera. 5) Moore 1959 and Ellerman 1940 used older generic limits (Aethosciurus = poensis, lucifer, vexillarius, ruwenzorii; Myrsilus/Allosciurus = Protoxerus aubinnii); species coverage above is mapped to MDD v2.5 names.
